decisions.what: Index plan approved: vehicle_time and account_updated re-keyed on tesla_id, account_time dropped with no replacement.

decisions.what: processor.go fans out over each account's vehicles now, keeping the account-keyed watermark.

decisions.what: SuperchargerHistoryByAccount and SuperchargerHistoryByAccountUpdatedSince are removed, not re-keyed.

decisions.what: In the mirror fan-out, one vehicle's failed read skips the whole account: no mirror write, no watermark advance.
decisions.why: The cursor covers every car of the account at once. Advancing it after a partial read would push it past the missing car's rows, losing them silently.

decisions.what: T-8's step past t3 is one microsecond, not one nanosecond. design.md, tasks.md and the test all corrected.
decisions.why: Postgres timestamptz holds microseconds and pgx truncates finer values, so t3+1ns reached the database as t3 and the inclusive bound correctly returned 7103. The design authored an unrepresentable value.

review.brief: Review RM57 tier 1: telemetry.supercharger_history re-keyed on tesla_id NOT NULL, account_id dropped, unregistered VINs skipped and counted. Read the branch diff against main, not the whole module. Gate items: (1) module boundaries - the worker touched only internal/telemetry; internal/app and internal/analytics are leader-owned integration, check they call ports only, never a telemetry table. (2) Every DB object matches the user-confirmed design gate RD6 - two tesla_id indexes created, the three old ones dropped, account_time replaced by nothing. A mismatch is a blocker. (3) Integration tests assert design.md's up-front expected values (T-1..T-10), not whatever the implementation happens to do. (4) SCRUTINIZE RD10: a design-authored expected value was corrected after a red test (t3+1ns -> t3+1us). Judge independently whether that is a legitimate correction of an unrepresentable value or a relaxed assertion. (5) Deleted tests - D3/D4 drop the account-wide port and 7 tests with it; confirm the lost coverage is genuinely obsolete and T-8/T-9 carry forward what survives. (6) Docs: AGENTS.md, the four kkpa/context guides, nothing edited under openspec/changes/archive/. (7) Read-heavy Performance-Profile compliance. (8) Anti-gaming: no weakened criteria, no self-approved statuses, tasks.md append-only. Signals: assistant ran build, vet, gofmt, migration/boundary/archive/vehicleref/money/tz guards - all clean. The OWNER ran make test and reported it passing; the assistant never ran the suite. Judge test quality by reading the tests, never by running them.

rounds.open_suite_question: The owner's last passing make test run predates commit 8cfcc4d. Everything that commit changed is one of: (a) doc/comment-only (F1-F4, L1 - zero runtime code touched), or (b) a parameter removed from collectChargingHistory that round 1 already established was dead in the function body, propagated to its one caller and four test call sites, all under the compiler's enforcement (go build and go vet both clean). A dead, unread parameter cannot change what a function computes; removing it and its call-site arguments in lockstep is a mechanically safe rewrite, not new or altered logic. The specific T-1..T-4 assertions I verified in round 1 are byte-for-byte unchanged in this commit - only their call syntax moved. On that basis I approve without waiting for a fresh make test: there is no plausible code path introduced since the owner's last green run that a suite run could catch and go vet did not. This judgment is contingent - if the owner's pending re-run comes back red, that overrides it immediately and the leader should re-open this round rather than treat the change as verified.
rounds.verdict_reasoning: All five round-1 findings and the leader's own L1 finding are genuinely fixed, independently re-verified against the files rather than the commit message. No new violation introduced by the fix commit. No blocker or major remains. Approved.
